crawler-scope.title: Begin with a crawl contract
crawler-scope.description: Seeds and a crawl budget lead to different outputs for indexing and archiving.
crawler-scope.note: Purpose determines what the crawler retains.

crawler-pipeline.title: A page becomes more work
crawler-pipeline.description: The frontier leases URLs, workers fetch, and parsing sends documents onward while links return to the frontier.
crawler-pipeline.note: The discovery loop must survive a worker crash.

crawler-policy.title: One host, one request budget
crawler-policy.description: Robots rules and a host-specific timer gate requests while unrelated hosts proceed.
crawler-policy.note: A fleet limit alone cannot protect one site.

crawler-frontier.title: Value meets eligibility
crawler-frontier.description: A priority selector chooses among host queues only when each host may be fetched.
crawler-frontier.note: Durable priority and host queues prevent starvation and floods.

crawler-dedup.title: Two identities, two checks
crawler-dedup.description: A normalized URL is checked before fetching; a content fingerprint is checked after fetching.
crawler-dedup.note: Keep URL history even when content bytes are shared.

crawler-fetch.title: Bound every network hop
crawler-fetch.description: DNS, redirects, byte limits, and a tolerant parser protect the downloader and its output.

crawler-freshness.title: Return when a page may change
crawler-freshness.description: Fetch history and validators set a recrawl time; errors and traps take bounded paths.
crawler-freshness.note: A 304 still updates the fetch history.

crawler-scale.title: Partition hosts, observe freshness
crawler-scale.description: Host queue ownership coordinates politeness while workers write documents and indexing events.
crawler-scale.note: More workers do not override a host's safe rate.
